newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African industrial shares on Friday ended weak in quiet trade ahead of the budget and the futures close-out. Golds were softer on a weak bullion price.
Dealers said the market was likely to remain weak ahead of the budget on Wednesday.
"The market was very quiet. There were no fireworks. I presume it will be quiet until the budget," a dealer said.
The main feature of the day was a 400,000 share bookover on De Beers at 1250 GMT, but dealers said overall volumes were light.
The March futures contract close-out on March 17 is also set to add to any budget-inspired volatility next week.
"(Next week) is the last week before the futures close-out and there are 50,000 open contracts. We will see some volatility next week," a dealer said.
Gold shares were seen drifting sideways next week as all market eyes would focus on the budget.
The all-share index shed 22.3 points to 7,061.9 points, the industrial index lost 26.4 points to 8,251.6 points, and the golds index dropped 13.5 points to 1,416.6 points.
De Beers ended up 50 cents to 156.50 rand, Anglo dropped 450 cents to 271 rand, RMB rose 25 cents to 94 rand. Sappi was a rand weaker at 33.50 rand.
Dries fell 110 cents to 45.60 rand, Freegold cut 30 cents to 35.20 rand and Amplats drops 150 cents to 34 rand.
Near-term share futures were also slightly weaker amid a lack of support from New York shares. Gold contracts were off on a struggling bullion price.
The all-share March contract was at 6,390/400 from 6,429 as the industrial contract dips to 7,887/900 from 7,954. The golds contract lay at 975/90 from 1003.
